pr.title: Plan answering an agent's questions from any host
pr.head: a3e5651d0b536fa94c02d6dee6797fbb86c1232e

summary: Projector's fix and review loops run subagents that sometimes need a decision only the person can make. Today a subagent hands its question to the main loop, which asks it as a line of text in the transcript. That line scrolls away, nothing lists which questions are still open, and nothing carries the answer back to the subagent.

This pull request adds one plan, docs/projects/questions/readme.md, at status: ready and priority: now. It changes no code. Earlier heads planned the feature inside Claude Code's band alone, under questions-drawer. This head moves the core into the project CLI so that every host reaches the same questions, and keeps the band as Claude Code's view.

1. An agent asks through the CLI. project question ask checks a one-line question with a required recommendation, numbers it, and writes it to the session's directory under Projector's state directory. Each question gets a fixed reference: #337.3 for the third question on #337, owner/repo#337.3 for another repository, or q2. In Claude Code, the mcp__projector__ask tool runs this command.
  2. You answer from the band or the CLI. Answers are lettered: a is always the recommendation, then the other options, and the last letter is a typed answer. The band shows each question under its pull request with a drawer of lettered choices, and project question answer #337.3.a answers from a terminal.
  3. The answer reaches the agent. The store records every answer first. Then one deliverer claims it under the lock with a token, renews the claim while the delivery waits, and marks it delivered or reopens it. In Claude Code the band is the deliverer for every answer in its session, sending to a live subagent or queueing for the main loop. Anywhere else project question watch prints each answer as one event line for a host's watcher. A reference typed in a prompt gets its question attached as context.
The rollout is two stacked pull requests: the CLI with its tests and docs first, then Claude Code's band and tool.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Projector's band: the strip above the Claude Code prompt that #267 added and /projector shows or hides.
  • Drawer: the extra lines that open under a band line when you press it.
  • Reference: a question's fixed name, #337.3, owner/repo#337.3, or q2, and an answer's, with its letter, #337.3.a.
  • Store: one directory per session under Projector's state directory, one JSON file per question, written under a lock.
  • watch: project question watch, which prints each undelivered answer as one line, the way Projector's loop watchers report GitHub events.

cards.title: Readiness
cards.html: The plan is new at ready and owns every open question. Section 7 lists five: a session's id outside Claude Code (owned, with an interim answer), the loop skills asking through the CLI (deferred), opening a pull request's drawer on the main screen (owned), views for Codex and Paseo (deferred), and old session directories (deferred). None blocks the two pull requests in the rollout.

groups.title: The questions plan
groups.kicker: One CLI that every host asks and answers through, with Claude Code's band as one view
intro: Sections 2.1 to 2.4 define the CLI: its commands, the store, the reference and letter scheme with the checks a question must pass, and how references are found in prompt text. Sections 2.5 to 2.7 define Claude Code's side: the ask tool that runs the CLI, what the band draws, and how the band delivers answers and attaches typed references.
Read § 2.7 with § 2.1's watch in mind. Together they decide which component delivers each answer.

checks.text: main now carries #267 and #269. Its hooks/types.d.ts declares bandDrawer beside the other band keys, and its hooks/register.tsx registers /projector and has the prompt.submit hook § 2.7 extends.
project check passes at this head. No file outside the plan refers to the old questions-drawer name.

files.note: The new plan: the CLI, its store and references, Claude Code's tool and band, the design reasons, acceptance tests, a two-step rollout, and open questions.

checks.text: Exit 65 for a refused question, a second answer, or a taken claim, 66 for an unknown reference, and 67 for a reference that names questions in two sessions match the meanings in docs/cli.md's exit-code table.
Writing to a temporary name and renaming, under a lock taken with O_EXCL, matches how src/projector/core.py and src/projector/review.py already write and lock with the standard library alone.

Under the lock, claim refuses a live claim, and renewing, marking delivered, and reopening each need the claim's own token. The band renews on every tick while a submit waits behind a busy main loop, so neither its next tick nor a watch takes the answer again.
The matching rule lets a reference close a sentence, and rejects #337.3.4, q2.4, and a bare 2, as the earlier review threads settled.
The tool turns exit 65 into a deny naming the failed check, and any other exit, such as 2 from an old CLI, into a deny that names project upgrade.
The tick reads the store whether the band is shown or not, which main's tick, returning early while hidden, needs changed. A question asked from the shell therefore shows a hidden band.
The band claims and delivers every answer its session's store holds without deliveredAt, so an answer given from a terminal reaches an agent in Claude Code with no watch running.

Each renewal rewrites the question's file, so the band's tick also runs list while a delivery waits. The token lives in the band's process, so a hot reload during a pending submit loses the renewals and can lead to a second copy a minute later. Both are review suggestions.
The live statuses here, pending, running, waiting, and idle, and the ended ones, completed, failed, and killed, are exactly the AgentStatus values in Claude Code 2.1.296's plugin API.
The "Record, then claim, then deliver" bullet now wraps at the plan's width, and no prose line in the plan stops short mid-paragraph or runs past it.
